screen.search_scope: Primary human studies and official data repositories relevant to participant-level pulmonary hemodynamics, regional perfusion, functional pulmonary capillary blood volume, pulmonary or capillary transit, hematological covariates, and joint measurement compatibility.
screen.outcome_boundary: Published abstracts, methods, tables, and figures were visible during source screening. No participant-level candidate data were obtained or inspected. New numeric acceptance limits must therefore be based on measurement repeatability, protocol uncertainty, and an independently reviewed clinical or physiological rationale, not tuned to published candidate outcomes.

measurement variables, units, and anatomical definitions
sample size, missingness, repeatability, and uncertainty
processing, publication, redistribution, and retention rights
independence from MEHLISSA calibration and existing validation sources
public outcome exposure before numeric tolerance locking

track_summary.conclusion: The University of Arizona healthy-control iCPET records remain the only screened source matching the primary recumbent multipoint mPAP-PAWP-cardiac-output tuple. Two upright cohorts can support a separately declared stress or generalization analysis. PVDOMICS healthy controls do not undergo invasive CPET under the published protocol and are rejected as the primary PCQ-H source unless a controlled variable inventory demonstrates otherwise.

The existing Bourhis five-lobe aggregate result remains supportive. Bailey is the closest five-lobe posture candidate, while Wong and Hopkins provide stronger dynamic-state designs but only four venous territories or right-lung spatial regions. Participant data and a predeclared mapping to the five MEHLISSA beds are still required.

D'Souza is the best primary-context candidate because functional capillary volume, cardiac output, and hemoglobin-adjusted measurements are stage matched in young semirecumbent adults. Lassen is the best screened whole-pulmonary transit and repeatability source but needs an anatomical observation model and cannot independently test its defining PBV equals flow times transit identity. Coffman provides a larger upright five-stage replication candidate with measured hemoglobin.

No screened cohort jointly measures the complete hemodynamic, five-lobe regional, functional capillary-volume, anatomically matched transit, and hematocrit state. D'Souza can support same-stage flow-volume coherence and a derived Vc/Q residence proxy; this remains a partial joint claim rather than complete PCQ-J qualification.

source.citation: Elliott J, Menakuru N, Martin KJ, et al. iCPET Calculator: A Web-Based Application to Standardize the Calculation of Alpha Distensibility in Patients With Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension. Journal of the American Heart Association. 2023;12:e029667.

candidates.population: Five reported healthy controls; the public supplement reports group age 43 plus or minus 16 years and 60 percent female. Individual age eligibility and the exact complete-stage count must be confirmed.
variables: optional systolic and diastolic pulmonary arterial pressure
candidates.jointness: The requested variables are stage matched within participant; at least three complete stages per accepted control remain to be confirmed.
candidates.uncertainty: Direct-Fick cardiac output and invasive pressure methods are reported; record-level measurement uncertainty and covariance are not public and must be requested or conservatively modelled.

access.route: Use the prepared UA iCPET request after institutional review.

candidates.article_license: article-specific open-access terms; verify at grant

independence.assessment: The institution and investigator group are distinct from the current Toronto, Leuven, Lee, Wolsk, Bourhis, Lewis, and Muehlfeld evidence roles; cohort disjointness must still be confirmed by the provider.

outcome_exposure.detail: The publication, public method description, and aggregate control age, sex, resting-pressure, alpha, and slope summaries were known before data access; no healthy-control participant trajectory has been inspected.

strengths: invasive stage-matched mPAP, PAWP, and cardiac output
already has a minimal pseudonymous request contract
gaps: group age 43 plus or minus 16 years may leave fewer participants inside the primary 20-to-40-year window
complete-stage count and uncertainty fields unconfirmed
candidates.decision_rationale: Best match to all three primary PCQ-H trajectory inputs in the declared posture.
candidates.next_action: Have an authorized institutional representative review and send docs/m3/UA_ICPET_DATA_REQUEST.md; do not inspect records until the PCQ-1.3 numeric amendment is committed.

source.citation: Coffman KE, Curry TB, Dietz NM, et al. The influence of pulmonary vascular pressures on lung diffusing capacity during incremental exercise in healthy aging. Physiological Reports. 2018;6:e13565.

candidates.population: Eighteen healthy adults, nine younger and nine older; invasive catheterization completed in four younger and five older participants.
variables: systolic and diastolic pulmonary arterial pressure
candidates.jointness: Seven repeated stages are available in the catheterized subset, with pressure, wedge pressure, and direct-Fick flow sampled within the same stage but at sequential time points.
candidates.uncertainty: Repeated stages and parallel direct-Fick and rebreathe flow support method checks; participant data, covariance, and raw waveform repeatability are not public.

access.participant_data: not publicly located; author request required
access.route: Confirm data retention, participant-level availability, and reuse terms with the study team.

independence.assessment: Not used to parameterize the frozen PCQ-1 candidates, but the Mayo research program overlaps authors and possibly participants with Coffman 2017; treat those two publications as one evidence family until audited.

outcome_exposure.detail: Published cohort results and methods were inspected; no participant trajectories were obtained.

gaps: pharmacological arm outside the primary claim
candidates.decision_rationale: Strong multipoint methodological backup and upright stress test, but not a posture-matched replacement for UA iCPET.
candidates.next_action: Request only if the primary UA path fails or an upright generalization protocol is approved; audit overlap with Coffman 2017 first.

source.citation: Pandey A, Kraus WE, Brubaker PH, Kitzman DW. Healthy Aging and Cardiovascular Function: Invasive Hemodynamics During Rest and Exercise in 104 Healthy Volunteers. JACC: Heart Failure. 2020;8:111-121.

candidates.population: One hundred four rigorously screened healthy volunteers aged 20 to 76 years.
candidates.posture: seated rest and upright exhaustive cycle exercise
candidates.jointness: Hemodynamic, gas-exchange, and imaging measurements were simultaneous by stage, but mPAP is not reported as an available endpoint in the source article and must not be assumed from catheter presence.
candidates.uncertainty: Large cohort and common protocol are strengths; the article states that legacy raw formats limit new individual-level analyses and published tables were digitized from historical plots.

access.participant_data: availability not established and legacy formats are limiting
access.route: Ask the corresponding author whether stage-level mPAP and participant records remain recoverable before any formal request.

independence.assessment: Duke historical cohort and investigators are distinct from the frozen candidate sources; no known overlap, subject to provider confirmation.

outcome_exposure.detail: Published aggregate age-stratified tables were visible; participant data were not inspected.

gaps: 1982-1989 source data and incompatible legacy formats
candidates.decision_rationale: Potential generalization resource, not currently eligible for the PCQ-H primary endpoint tuple.
candidates.next_action: Perform a feasibility-only author inquiry after the higher-ranked requests if mPAP and stage-level records are still required.

source.citation: Tang WHW, Wilcox JD, Jacob MS, et al. Comprehensive Diagnostic Evaluation of Cardiovascular Physiology in Patients With Pulmonary Vascular Disease: Insights From the PVDOMICS Program. Circulation: Heart Failure. 2020.

candidates.population: PVDOMICS includes pulmonary vascular disease groups, disease comparators, and healthy controls.
candidates.posture: upright at most centers and supine at Mayo; healthy-control invasive exercise is not part of the published protocol
states: invasive CPET for selected pulmonary-hypertension participants
candidates.jointness: The published methods specify non-invasive CPET for healthy controls; they therefore do not establish the required healthy stage-matched mPAP-PAWP-cardiac-output trajectory.
candidates.uncertainty: Standardized multicenter forms exist, but center, posture, phenotype, and protocol heterogeneity require controlled variable-level review.

access.route: dbGaP study phs002451.v1.p1 with Data Use Certification
access.redistribution: restricted by repository and consent terms

independence.assessment: The multicenter network includes Arizona and Mayo sites represented in other screened candidates; site and cohort lineage must be checked before any later use.

outcome_exposure.detail: Protocol and official repository metadata were inspected, not participant outcomes.

gaps: healthy controls receive non-invasive rather than invasive CPET
candidates.decision_rationale: Does not meet the published PCQ-H healthy invasive trajectory requirement; retained only for later non-invasive covariates or generalization.
candidates.next_action: Do not submit a PCQ-H primary request unless the dbGaP variable inventory proves that eligible healthy invasive stages exist.

source.citation: Kovacs G, et al. Pulmonary hemodynamics during exercise and prognosis in the PEX-NET registry. European Respiratory Journal. 2024.

candidates.population: Large clinically referred international exercise-hemodynamics registry rather than a narrow healthy-volunteer cohort.
candidates.jointness: Repeated invasive hemodynamics exist, but protocol and phenotype heterogeneity prevent silent use as the primary healthy-recumbent cohort.
candidates.uncertainty: Large sample supports later stress testing; between-center method and selection heterogeneity must be modeled.

independence.assessment: A multicenter registry may include cohorts or investigators represented by current aggregate sources; source lineage must be resolved before use.

outcome_exposure.detail: Registry-level publication summaries were known; no participant records were inspected.

candidates.decision_rationale: Useful only under a separate generalization design after the narrow PCQ-H evaluation.
candidates.next_action: Retain for a later external stress-test protocol, not PCQ-1.3 primary selection.

source.citation: Bourhis D, Robin P, Essalah A, Abgral R. V/Q SPECT for the Assessment of Regional Lung Function: Generation of Normal Mean and Standard Deviation 3-D Maps. Frontiers in Medicine. 2020;7:143.

candidates.population: Seventy-three clinically referred examinations judged strictly normal by two nuclear physicians.
variables: five relative lobe perfusion fractions with and without attenuation correction
candidates.jointness: Only aggregate lobe means are in the repository; both reconstruction series share the same cohort.
candidates.uncertainty: Published lobe means and reconstruction sensitivity are available; participant-level covariance is absent locally.

access.redistribution: participant records not permitted or obtained

independence.assessment: Already used as the source-disjoint aggregate validation of the Lee-derived fixed lobe shares and therefore not a new independent PCQ-R cohort.

outcome_exposure.detail: This is an already executed MEHLISSA aggregate validation source.

gaps: cannot count as new PCQ-R validation
candidates.decision_rationale: Retained as existing evidence and reproduction control, not promoted to participant-level PCQ-R qualification.
candidates.next_action: Reproduce unchanged during PCQ-1.6 and seek a distinct participant-level or dynamic cohort.

source.citation: Bailey DL, Farrow CE, Lau EM. V/Q SPECT-Normal Values for Lobar Function and Comparison With CT Volumes. Seminars in Nuclear Medicine. 2019;49:58-61.

candidates.population: Small cohort of normal subjects; exact participant count and eligibility details require full-text or author confirmation.
candidates.posture: radiotracer administered in supine and erect conditions; SPECT/CT acquired supine
variables: relative functional contribution of all five lung lobes
candidates.jointness: Five lobe contributions and posture are reported within the study, but participant-level pairing and covariance are not publicly established.
candidates.uncertainty: Normal ranges are reported; raw participant uncertainty, acquisition repeatability, and exact sample size require confirmation.

access.article: abstract public; full article access may be restricted
access.participant_data: not publicly located; author request required
access.route: Contact the corresponding author for a minimal lobe-by-posture extract and rights statement.

independence.assessment: Australian investigators and cohort are distinct from the Lee calibration and Bourhis validation sources; this must be confirmed by recruitment and upstream-data audit.

outcome_exposure.detail: Abstract-level direction and methods were inspected; participant lobe values were not obtained.

gaps: small and incompletely described public sample
injection posture and acquisition posture must remain distinct
candidates.decision_rationale: Closest screened source to participant-level five-lobe posture qualification.
candidates.next_action: Prepare an author feasibility request after confirming the full article metadata; require participant-level five-lobe fractions, posture labels, uncertainty, and reuse terms.

source.citation: Wong DTH, Lee KJ, Yoo SJ, Tomlinson G, Grosse-Wortmann L. Changes in systemic and pulmonary blood flow distribution in normal adult volunteers in response to posture and exercise: a phase contrast magnetic resonance imaging study. Journal of Physiological Sciences. 2014;64:105-112.

candidates.population: Twenty-four healthy adult volunteers without known cardiac or respiratory abnormality.
candidates.posture: prone rest, supine rest, and supine cycle exercise
variables: right and left pulmonary artery flow
right upper and lower pulmonary vein flow
left upper and lower pulmonary vein flow
candidates.jointness: Vessel flows are repeated within participant and condition; right middle pulmonary venous drainage is incorporated into the right lower pulmonary vein territory when separately present.
candidates.uncertainty: Published means and standard deviations are available; participant covariance and vessel-level repeatability require raw data or provider estimates.

access.participant_data: not publicly located; author request required
access.route: Ask whether de-identified per-condition vessel flows and right-middle drainage anatomy remain available.

independence.assessment: Toronto pediatric/cardiac imaging investigators and cohort are distinct from the current Lee and Bourhis regional sources; recruitment lineage must still be confirmed.

outcome_exposure.detail: Published aggregate vessel-flow tables and directional results were inspected; participant records were not.

strengths: cardiac output and pulmonary vessel partition in one protocol
gaps: four venous drainage territories rather than five anatomical lobes
right middle lobe may be combined with right lower territory
candidates.decision_rationale: Best screened dynamic regional-flow backup, but it can support only an explicitly aggregated observation model.
candidates.next_action: Use only after PCQ-1.3 freezes a four-territory observation model that combines MEHLISSA right-middle and right-lower predictions.

source.citation: Hall ET, Sa RC, Holverda S, et al. The effect of supine exercise on the distribution of regional pulmonary blood flow measured using proton MRI. Journal of Applied Physiology. 2014;116:451-461.

candidates.population: Six healthy adults, four men and two women, mean age 32 plus or minus 6 years.
candidates.jointness: Rest and exercise imaging are repeated within participant, but spatial slices and gravitational regions are not anatomical lobe measurements.
candidates.uncertainty: Regional variability is reported; small sample, right-lung-only imaging, breath timing, and mapping uncertainty dominate translation to MEHLISSA beds.

access.participant_data: not publicly located; author request required
access.route: Use as method and dynamic-pattern context unless raw regional maps and rights are granted.

independence.assessment: UC San Diego cohort and imaging approach are distinct from current regional parameterization and validation sources.

outcome_exposure.detail: Published aggregate patterns were inspected; participant images and values were not obtained.

candidates.decision_rationale: Useful as a dynamic spatial stress test after a separate observation model, not a direct PCQ-R1 five-lobe source.
candidates.next_action: Retain as method context; do not prioritize over Bailey or Wong for PCQ-1.

source.citation: D'Souza AW, Brotto AR, Hicks B, et al. Pulmonary capillary blood volume and diffusing membrane capacity during exercise in humans: role of pulmonary artery pressure. American Journal of Physiology-Lung Cellular and Molecular Physiology. 2025;328:L631-L637.

candidates.population: Fifteen healthy nonsmoking young adults, seven female, age 24 plus or minus 4 years; cardiac output available for fourteen and RVSP for six.
candidates.posture: baseline and 60 W semirecumbent cycle exercise
states: 60 W exercise with bilateral thigh cuffs at 90 mmHg
variables: functional pulmonary capillary blood volume Vc
right ventricular systolic pressure in a subset
candidates.jointness: Vc and cardiac output are measured in the same participant and state for fourteen participants. RVSP is available in six. No PAWP or directly measured mPAP is available, and Vc divided by flow would be a derived functional residence proxy rather than a measured anatomical transit time.
candidates.uncertainty: The multiple-inspired-oxygen Vc regression requires r-squared at least 0.95 and values are hemoglobin adjusted. Record-level repeatability, covariance, missingness, and the distinction between measurement error and biological variation must be requested.

access.participant_data: available from corresponding author on reasonable request
access.redistribution: not established separately from article licence

independence.assessment: University of Alberta cohort and authors are distinct from the Lewis functional-volume parameter source and the frozen pulmonary calibration and validation sources. Cohort overlap with other Alberta papers must be confirmed.

outcome_exposure.detail: Published group and plotted individual outcomes were visible during screening. Raw records were not inspected; numeric tolerances may not be tuned to the visible results.

gaps: only three states with two distinct exercise interventions
candidates.decision_rationale: Best screened match for independent functional capillary-volume qualification and partial flow-volume coherence.
candidates.next_action: Review and send the prepared minimal request; obtain rights and a data dictionary, then lock the Vc observation equation, hemoglobin handling, missingness rule, and numeric tolerance before record access.

source.citation: Coffman KE, Carlson AR, Miller AD, Johnson BD, Taylor BJ. The effect of aging and cardiorespiratory fitness on the lung diffusing capacity response to exercise in healthy humans. Journal of Applied Physiology. 2017;122:1425-1434.

candidates.population: Thirty-one healthy adults: sixteen young adults aged 22 to 30 and fifteen older adults aged 60 to 76, stratified by fitness.
variables: functional pulmonary capillary blood volume Vc
candidates.jointness: Duplicate Vc, diffusing-capacity, cardiac-output, and measured-hemoglobin observations are available within participant at five stages. Vc and cardiac output share one rebreathing procedure, which may induce correlated method error.
candidates.uncertainty: Duplicate measurements and measured hemoglobin are important strengths; raw replicate covariance and participant values are not publicly downloadable, and the article manuscript has restricted reuse terms.

access.article: accepted manuscript available for private research under repository terms
access.participant_data: not publicly located; author request required
access.route: Request minimal stage-level and replicate data plus explicit reuse terms from the corresponding author.

candidates.article_license: publisher copyright; repository copy is not openly relicensable

independence.assessment: Not used in the frozen candidate, but shares Mayo investigators and potentially participants with Coffman 2018. It is independent from D'Souza and current Lewis calibration only after cohort confirmation.

outcome_exposure.detail: Published figures, group statistics, and methods were inspected; participant-stage records were not obtained.

strengths: young primary-age subset and older generalization subset
gaps: shared rebreathing method can correlate Vc and flow errors
candidates.decision_rationale: Strong replication and uncertainty source after D'Souza, but posture and evidence-family overlap prevent it from replacing the primary candidate silently.
candidates.next_action: Audit cohort overlap with Coffman 2018 and request only under a separately declared upright replication or generalization analysis.

source.citation: Lassen ML, Byrne C, et al. Pulmonary blood volume assessment from a standard cardiac rubidium-82 imaging protocol: impact of adenosine-induced hyperemia. Journal of Nuclear Cardiology. 2023;30:2504-2513.

candidates.population: Thirty-three young healthy volunteers, fifteen female, median age 23 years; twenty-five had successful test-retest sessions.
variables: mean bolus transit time from pulmonary trunk to left atrium
cardiac output derived as stroke volume times heart rate
pulmonary blood volume derived as cardiac output times mean bolus transit time
candidates.jointness: Transit and cardiac output are measured or derived in the same scan. Pulmonary blood volume is defined algebraically as flow times transit and therefore cannot independently validate volume-flow-transit closure.
candidates.uncertainty: Test-retest repeatability coefficients and smallest real differences are reported. Rubidium retention may prolong transit by about 25 percent, stroke volume lacks an independent imaging reference, and the threshold-based arrival definition is method specific.

access.participant_data: not publicly located; author request required
access.route: Ask for de-identified rest, stress, and replicate MBTT, HR, SV, and body-size records plus reuse terms.

independence.assessment: Copenhagen PET cohort and investigators are distinct from the Swift transit calibration and all screened functional Vc sources; upstream cohort reuse must still be confirmed.

outcome_exposure.detail: Published means, repeatability, and method limitations were inspected; participant scans and values were not obtained.

gaps: adenosine is outside the primary resting state
PBV is definitionally Q times transit
candidates.decision_rationale: Best screened source for PCQ-C2 observation-model and tolerance development, but not an independent test of joint closure.
candidates.next_action: Seek participant-level MBTT data and use the published repeatability only after PCQ-1.3 freezes a pulmonary-trunk-to-left-atrium observation model and explicitly excludes circular PBV closure as validation evidence.

source.citation: Tedjasaputra V, van Diepen S, Collins SE, et al. Assessment of Pulmonary Capillary Blood Volume, Membrane Diffusing Capacity, and Intrapulmonary Arteriovenous Anastomoses During Exercise. Journal of Visualized Experiments. 2017;(120):54949.

candidates.population: Representative healthy exercise measurement demonstration; not a validation cohort.
variables: functional pulmonary capillary blood volume Vc
candidates.jointness: Representative data illustrate the measurement workflow but do not constitute an independent participant-level validation data set.
candidates.uncertainty: Useful for method steps and assumptions; no qualifying cohort precision or independent test split.

access.route: Use only to document the Vc observation method.

independence.assessment: Shares University of Alberta methods lineage with D'Souza and cannot be counted as an independent cohort.

gaps: not independent of the Alberta evidence family
